title: Closed-Form Time–Strain Solution for Creep and Relaxation of Clays Under a Rate-Dependent Isotache Law: Bounds on Cα/Cc and Design Times
content: In the isotache law of Watabe and co-workers, the preconsolidation pressure has a lower limit, so creep at constant stress is bounded. Its time–strain curve was known only numerically. This paper derives it in closed form: for a locally log-linear reference curve, the time to reach a given strain is an incomplete beta function. The strain approaches its bound as a power of time with exponent c₂/(1 − c₂) ≈ 0.12, c₂ being the rate exponent. The log-time ratio Cα/Cc lies between two bounds and decreases strictly, so the curve is concave in log time; from the formal origin, it falls from 0.048 to 0.030 as the strain rate drops from 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻⁸ s⁻¹. In 18 long-term oedometer tests on clays outside the calibration set, the solution with published parameters and no fitting was more accurate than the generic ratio Cα/Cc = 0.04 in 17; a power law without lower limit did similarly. With one parameter, the level of the lower limit, fitted to a complete test, it predicted other stresses of the same clay with a median error of 0.19% strain, against 0.29% for a power law and 0.40% for a Cα/Cc ratio calibrated on the same test.
